title: The Galois Closure of ℚ(⁴√2) is ℚ(⁴√2, i): [ℚ(⁴√2, i) : ℚ] = 8
description: Answers the parent ⁴√2 entry's open question OQ-01: what is the Galois closure of ℚ(⁴√2)? Since X⁴ − 2 has the non-real roots ±i·⁴√2, its splitting field is ℚ(⁴√2, i). This entry formalizes the DEGREE and the field-theoretic structure of that closure. Working inside ℂ with ⁴√2 modeled as the real number √√2, it proves the quadratic tower ℚ ⊂ ℚ(⁴√2) ⊂ ℚ(⁴√2, i), with the bottom step of degree 4 (from the parent) and the top step of degree 2, giving [ℚ(⁴√2, i) : ℚ] = 8. The crux is the STRICT second step i ∉ ℚ(⁴√2): the closure genuinely enlarges the field. This is captured by packaging the reals as an explicit intermediate field realIF (the complex numbers with zero imaginary part): ℚ(⁴√2) is generated by the real ⁴√2, so it lies inside ℝ, whereas i does not — so i cannot already be present. The four roots ±⁴√2, ±i·⁴√2 all lie in the closure, so X⁴ − 2 splits there. Zero axioms, zero sorries, no native_decide. The full identification of the Galois group with the dihedral group D₄ is left as a follow-up.

originalContributions: finrank_galois_closure: the exact degree [ℚ(⁴√2, i) : ℚ] = 8 of the Galois closure of ℚ(⁴√2), the quantitative heart of the parent's OQ-01. Obtained from the tower law applied to ℚ ⊂ ℚ(⁴√2) ⊂ ℚ(⁴√2, i) with steps of degree 4 and 2.

I_not_mem_adjoin_a: the CRUX — i ∉ ℚ(⁴√2). This is what makes the closure proper (degree 8 rather than 4). Proved by packaging the reals as an intermediate field realIF ⊂ ℂ and showing ℚ(⁴√2) ≤ realIF (the generator ⁴√2 is real), while Im(i) = 1 ≠ 0.

realIF / realSubfield: the reals ℝ realized as an explicit IntermediateField ℚ ℂ (numbers with zero imaginary part), the device that turns 'ℚ(⁴√2) is real' into a usable field-theoretic bound ℚ(⁴√2) ≤ realIF.
minpoly_I / finrank_step_two: X² + 1 is the minimal polynomial of i over ℚ(⁴√2) (irreducible there because it has no real root), so [ℚ(⁴√2, i) : ℚ(⁴√2)] = 2 — the strict second step of the tower.
minpoly_a / finrank_adjoin_a: transports the parent's degree-4 result for the real ⁴√2 to the complex embedding a = (⁴√2 : ℂ), giving minpoly ℚ a = X⁴ − 2 and [ℚ(⁴√2) : ℚ] = 4 inside ℂ.

roots_mem_closure / I_mul_a_pow_four: the four roots ±⁴√2, ±i·⁴√2 of X⁴ − 2 (each satisfying z⁴ = 2 since i⁴ = 1) all lie in ℚ(⁴√2, i), so the polynomial splits over the closure — the splitting-field property.

overview.historicalContext: The parent entry fourth-root-2-irrational proves that ⁴√2 has degree exactly 4 over ℚ, by Eisenstein's criterion at the prime 2 on X⁴ − 2 followed by Gauss's lemma. But ℚ(⁴√2) is NOT a normal (Galois) extension of ℚ: it contains the real root ⁴√2 of X⁴ − 2 yet misses the two non-real roots ±i·⁴√2. The Galois closure — the smallest normal extension containing ℚ(⁴√2) — is the splitting field of X⁴ − 2, namely ℚ(⁴√2, i). This is the classic first nontrivial example of a non-normal radical extension and of a Galois group that is neither cyclic nor abelian: Gal(ℚ(⁴√2, i)/ℚ) ≅ D₄, the dihedral group of order 8 (symmetries of a square, matching the square arrangement of the four roots in ℂ).
overview.problemStatement:
**Open Question (parent fourth-root-2-irrational, OQ-01)**: what is the Galois closure of ℚ(⁴√2)? Since X⁴ − 2 has the non-real roots ±i·⁴√2, the splitting field is ℚ(⁴√2, i) of degree 8 with Galois group D₄ — a natural next formalization.

**This entry**: proves the DEGREE and field-theoretic structure — [ℚ(⁴√2, i) : ℚ] = 8 via the tower ℚ ⊂ ℚ(⁴√2) ⊂ ℚ(⁴√2, i), the crux being the strict step i ∉ ℚ(⁴√2); and that all four roots lie in the closure so X⁴ − 2 splits there.
overview.text: A 229-line, fully verified file (0 sorries, 0 axioms, no native_decide) importing Mathlib and the parent degree-4 result. It works inside ℂ, modeling ⁴√2 as the real √√2 coerced to ℂ and adjoining i = Complex.I. The tower is assembled from two degree computations — [ℚ(⁴√2):ℚ] = 4 (transported from the parent) and [ℚ(⁴√2, i):ℚ(⁴√2)] = 2 — combined via the tower law.
overview.proofStrategy: (1) Transport the parent's degree-4 fact into ℂ: with a = (⁴√2 : ℂ), a⁴ = 2, and X⁴ − 2 is irreducible over ℚ (parent), so minpoly ℚ a = X⁴ − 2 and [ℚ(a):ℚ] = 4 (IntermediateField.adjoin.finrank). (2) Package the reals as an intermediate field realIF ⊂ ℂ (zero imaginary part), a genuine Subfield.toIntermediateField. Since the generator a is real, ℚ(a) ≤ realIF (adjoin_le_iff). (3) The crux I_not_mem_adjoin_a: if i ∈ ℚ(a) ≤ realIF then Im(i) = 0, contradicting Im(i) = 1. (4) i is integral over ℚ(a) with X² + 1 as minimal polynomial: X² + 1 has no root in ℚ(a) (a root would be real with square −1, impossible), so it is irreducible there (degree ≤ 3, no root), giving [ℚ(a)(i):ℚ(a)] = 2. (5) The tower law Module.finrank_mul_finrank yields [ℚ(a)(i):ℚ] = 4·2 = 8, and adjoin_simple_adjoin_simple identifies ℚ(a)(i) with ℚ(a, i). (6) Finally the four roots ±a, ±i·a (each with fourth power 2, since i⁴ = 1) all lie in ℚ(a, i), so X⁴ − 2 splits over the closure.
keyInsights: ℚ(⁴√2) is real; its Galois closure is not: the entire obstruction to normality is that ℚ(⁴√2) ⊂ ℝ misses the imaginary unit. Realizing ℝ as an explicit intermediate field realIF turns this geometric fact into the one-line field-theoretic bound ℚ(⁴√2) ≤ realIF that powers the crux i ∉ ℚ(⁴√2).

The degree is a product of two independent steps: [ℚ(⁴√2):ℚ] = 4 (irreducibility of X⁴ − 2, from the parent) times [ℚ(⁴√2, i):ℚ(⁴√2)] = 2 (i satisfies the irreducible X² + 1 over the real field ℚ(⁴√2)). The tower law multiplies them to 8.

Irreducibility of X² + 1 over ℚ(⁴√2) reduces to 'no root': a degree-2 polynomial over a field is irreducible iff it has no root, and a root here would be a real number whose square is −1 — impossible. No abstract normality argument is needed.

The four roots ±⁴√2, ±i·⁴√2 sit at the vertices of a square in ℂ; the Galois group D₄ is exactly the symmetry group of that square. This entry secures the degree (= |D₄| = 8) and the splitting property; naming the group structure D₄ is the natural follow-up.

conclusion.summary: The Galois closure of ℚ(⁴√2) is the splitting field ℚ(⁴√2, i), and [ℚ(⁴√2, i) : ℚ] = 8. The degree is the product of two tower steps — [ℚ(⁴√2):ℚ] = 4 (parent, via Eisenstein) and [ℚ(⁴√2, i):ℚ(⁴√2)] = 2 — the second step being strict precisely because ℚ(⁴√2) is real (packaged as the intermediate field realIF) whereas i is not. All four roots ±⁴√2, ±i·⁴√2 lie in the closure, so X⁴ − 2 splits there. Zero axioms, zero sorries.
conclusion.implications: This is the classic first example of a radical extension whose Galois closure is strictly larger and whose Galois group is non-abelian (D₄). The entry secures the quantitative content — the degree 8 = |D₄| and the splitting property — on which the group-theoretic description rests, and demonstrates a reusable pattern: realizing ℝ as an explicit intermediate field to certify that a real subfield of ℂ omits i.
openQuestions: Identify Gal(ℚ(⁴√2, i)/ℚ) explicitly with the dihedral group D₄: construct the 8 field automorphisms (generated by the order-4 map ⁴√2 ↦ i·⁴√2, i ↦ i and the order-2 complex conjugation) and prove the group isomorphism.
Prove ℚ(⁴√2, i) is Galois over ℚ (normal + separable) via IsSplittingField of the separable X⁴ − 2, and derive card(Gal) = 8 from IsGalois.card_aut_eq_finrank.

Compute the lattice of intermediate fields of ℚ(⁴√2, i)/ℚ and match it (by the Galois correspondence) with the subgroup lattice of D₄, exhibiting the three degree-2 subfields and the non-normal ℚ(⁴√2).
